chess-terminology.note: Meta-record of the naming discipline: name_status, the refusal to coin terms for detector tags, and the five deliberately unclaimed motifs.

notation.note: Four systems and why they differ; all four are in use in this codebase.

board-geometry.note: Colour-boundedness, the knight's colour change, and the rule of the square with a tablebase-proven side-to-move pair.

piece-properties.note: The point count typed as a rule of thumb, with the bishop/knight dispute and a proven-draw counterexample a bishop and pawn up.

ranks-files-diagonals.note: Lines as what long-range pieces actually contest, and pawns as the only thing that opens or closes a file.

tactical-combinations.note: Written as a contested definition: four named authorities, a failed 1952 consensus attempt, and Averbakh arguing both sides four years apart.

forcing-moves.note: Written as a search-ordering rule with an explicit refusal to treat forcing as evidence of quality.

calculation-principles.note: calculation written, covering forcing-moves-first, breadth before depth, and the human pruning limit.

candidate-moves.note: candidate-moves written, recording the Kotov/Nunn/Dvoretsky dispute rather than resolving it in Kotov's favour.

planning.note: Written as guidance with the three standard failure modes named; the Steinitz link recorded as association, not attribution.

positional-evaluation.note: Steinitz's accumulation theory plus the permanent/temporary element lists, flagged as a later refinement rather than his own words.

defensive-principles.note: Written with the simplify-vs-complicate conflict recorded rather than resolved, plus the Paulsen attribution finding.

piece-activity.note: Written as the general case most other positional concepts specialise, with the activity/material exchange rate taken from this base's own gambit measurements.

piece-coordination.note: Written with an explicit prohibition on using it as a fallback label; it is the least detectable concept in this base and says so.

worst-placed-piece.note: Written with the four-way attribution dispute intact (Anderssen / Makogonov / Fischer / Dvoretsky) and with the precondition both original formulations carry.

pawn-breaks.note: pawn-breakthrough and minority-attack. The latter was a gap the final-phase brief named and the base did not have.

transformation-of-advantages.note: Written from Dvoretsky & Yusupov's Technique in Chess, including the authors' own statement that concrete play runs contrary to their golden principles, and a published objection to that framing.

opening-principles.note: early-queen-development written with a controlled engine measurement; opening-development, center-control, castling and tempo already existed.

opening-theory-concepts.note: transposition, theoretical-novelty, tabiya, opening-repertoire. Three of the four are not detectable without an opening database, which is recorded on each.

gambit-principles.note: gambit and compensation, both validated against the controlled searchmoves spectrum.

middlegame-principles.note: Umbrella; records that the phase has a procedure rather than a rule set.

endgame-principles.note: Umbrella record of Shereshevsky's four principles, with the point that the endgame is the one phase where claims can be proven.

king-activation.note: Written with a tablebase pair measuring the king's defensive value (dtm 35 vs 15) and with Shereshevsky's own documented rook-ending exception.

rook-endgames.note: rook-endgame-principles, deliberately an umbrella of caveats: three standard rules have proven counterexamples in this base.

knight-endgames.note: Botvinnik's formula, with the standard reference's own admission that knight-vs-knight-and-pawn has no operative principles.

queen-endgames.note: Orientation only; the class resisted complete human analysis until tablebases, and the record says to look positions up rather than reason about them.

mixed-piece-endgames.note: Orientation only, and says the class is under-researched here.

named-strategic-concepts.note: Meta-record of this base's attribution findings.

historical-principles.note: What happens to old principles: condition lost, disproved, or quantified.

modern-dynamic.note: Watson's thesis, corroborated independently by the cognitive-psychology literature.

exceptions-to-rules.note: Meta-record of this base's structural commitment that every soft-typed concept records where it fails; enforced by the test suite.

beginner-misconceptions.note: Meta-record indexing what this base has established that people wrongly believe; backed by the generated warnings index.

intermediate-concepts.note: Meta; difficulty is about the concept, not the player.

advanced-concepts.note: Meta; dependency rather than difficulty, and the tier this system detects worst.

practical-principles.note: The objective/practical distinction, kept small deliberately.

how_to_resume: 1. Read education/README.md, then ARCHITECTURE.md and METHODOLOGY.md.
2. Run: python3 tools/validate_kb.py && python3 tools/run_tests.py && node tests/test_api.js && python3 tools/corpus_check.py && node tools/trap_audit.js
3. Artifacts: state/COMPLETION.md (ten criteria), state/ladder.json, state/TRAPS.md, state/firing_rates.json, state/pawn_endings.json, state/breakthrough_proof.json, state/COVERAGE.md.
4. THE READING LIST IS THE ENGINE. `node tools/trap_audit.js --unread` lists every condition a record states that nobody has written about. 47 of 246 remain. Twenty-five defects have come out of it.

5. THE TOOL CREDITS BY QUOTATION AND QUOTING IS CHEAP. Twenty-two rows were closed in one pass by READING them against the code and quoting the guard where it already lived - that is legitimate only because each was checked first. Four `implements` strings have been found claiming something the code does not do, which is what the habit is for.

6. `indicators_against` DOES NOT MEAN THE SAME THING ON EVERY RECORD. On a concept naming an ASSET they are reasons not to report it; on one naming a SCALE or a liability (king-safety, isolated-queen-pawn) they are the conditions the matcher fires ON. Several are also the NEGATION of a precondition and cannot arise at all.

7. THREE ANSWERS TO A CONDITION, and the third keeps being right: build it, argue on the record that it cannot be built, or SAY IT IN THE SENTENCE. Nine times now a guard was written, measured, found to delete a canonical position, and replaced by a clause.

8. WHEN A GUARD DELETES A CANONICAL POSITION, THE GUARD IS WRONG. Rubinstein-Salwe, Capablanca-Tartakower, Capablanca-Rubinstein, Havasi-Capablanca, Lisitsin-Capablanca, Fischer-Spassky g6, Nimzowitsch-Capablanca, the three-against-three. Run corpus_check.py before and after every change.

9. FOUR corpus entries carry a written self-assessment: three RECORDED FAILURES kept failing on purpose (Reti-Capablanca piece-activity, Ftacnik-Roiz bishop-pair confidence, Karpov-Polgar rook-on-the-seventh false positive) and one - Anand-Leko blockade - that grades its own evidence DOWN because the raw feature is absent too. Do not fix any of them with a rule fitted to one position.
10. Confidence has TWO ceilings: knowledge_type and each record's own typical_confidence. Nothing may report above its record. If a record's figure is wrong, correct the record with an argument.

11. The largest remaining gap is criterion 4: 77% of applicable concepts have no negative example and 79% no ambiguous one. They come from articles by named authors ABOUT the failure mode - seven corpus entries from five such articles so far.
what_worked_this_session: Reading a condition against the code before crediting it. Twenty-two rows closed that way, and none of them by loosening the test.
Saying a condition in the sentence when building it as a guard would delete a canonical position. Nine times now, and it is the answer more often than a guard is.
Noticing when a matcher HAD the fact and did not say the word - rook-on-the-seventh knew whether the king was confined and never used Nimzowitsch's vocabulary for it.
Letting a build expose a bug in neighbouring code: the battery ordering was backwards, and only writing the 'expensive way round' clause revealed it.

failed_research_attempts.item: controlled pair isolating king activity in a rook ending
failed_research_attempts.detail: Two designs tried, both failed to split. Pair 1 (defending king e7 vs a7 in R+P vs R) came out win/win, though with dtm 35 vs 15, which was kept as a measurement of defensive value. Pair 2 (Philidor setup, defending king e7 vs g7) came out draw/draw - the rook on the sixth holds regardless of the king's square. Consistent with the three failed outpost pairs and with Shereshevsky's own remark that rook endings are too concrete for the principle to isolate.
failed_research_attempts.conclusion: Recorded on the king-activation concept as a limitation; the concept claims only what the win/win pair measured.

failed_research_attempts.detail: The score printed in the UMBC lecture notes does not replay: Black's 24th move (Ra3) is not legal in the position reached. The first 46 plies verify. Rather than guess a correction, only the verified prefix is used and the source note says so.
failed_research_attempts.conclusion: Verified prefix used; the remainder is neither used nor cited.

failed_research_attempts.what: Grounding `backward-pawn` on Marshall-Tarrasch, Nuremberg 1905, which a FIDE Master's annotation presents as 'the backward pawn on the semi-open file' and makes the title of its lesson
failed_research_attempts.result: REJECTED - the pawn is not backward by the definition this base uses, and the annotation's own stated reason describes a pawn that is not on the board
failed_research_attempts.reason: The annotation says White 'is left with a backward pawn on a semi-open file' after the exchange on c3, and explains it as 'the b2 and d4 pawns sit on adjacent files blocking its advance'. After 11.bxc3 there IS no b2 pawn - it is the pawn that captured on c3 - and c4 is empty and controlled by no black pawn, so c3 can advance freely. The record's definition, taken from Wikipedia and stated in its preconditions, requires BOTH halves: behind its neighbours AND unable to advance safely. This base's detector reports no backward pawn at any ply of the relevant sequence, and it is right. The pawn is a weak pawn on a half-open file, which is a different and weaker claim than the one the lesson is named after. Recorded rather than added: the corpus is ground truth, and grounding a concept on a loose application of its own definition would poison exactly the thing it exists to protect.
failed_research_attempts.conclusion: backward-pawn still needs human grounding. Look for an annotation that names the square in FRONT of the pawn as the point, which is the half of the concept that makes it matter and the half a loose usage always omits.

tool_limitations.tool: background shell scripts (Bash run_in_background + until-loop waiters)
limits: A waiter polling for a sentinel is only safe if the producing script writes that sentinel UNCONDITIONALLY. If a step raises, the script dies before the echo and the waiter spins forever. Use `trap 'echo DONE_X' EXIT` at the top of the script, not a bare echo at the bottom.
Renaming or rerunning an analysis under a different output filename orphans any waiter still watching the old one. Kill the waiter or reuse the filename.
Orphaned waiters are harmless — idle sleep loops — but they are invisible in ps output unless you grep for the loop body rather than for the analysis tool.

tool_limitations.note: theoretical-novelty, tabiya and gambit identification all require a game database the Education System does not have. Recorded on each concept as a limitation rather than left for a caller to discover.

tool_limitations.item: warnings index does not grade its own evidence
tool_limitations.note: state/warnings_index.json compiles 826 warnings but does not distinguish those proven by tablebase or controlled measurement from those resting on source authority. A caller cannot currently tell a proof from an opinion. Recorded as a known gap on both meta-concepts.

tool_limitations.item: detector claims were unverified until now
tool_limitations.note: For most of this project a concept could claim a mechanical detector that did not exist, because the audit compared against a list rather than the code. Fixed; the check now reads lib/*.js, blind-chess.html and tools/*.js.

Mass testing runs on 788 tactical puzzles because that is the corpus this repository has. The positional half of the system would be better judged on quiet middlegame positions, and no such labelled corpus exists here.

Six of seven 'full move order' listings printed by an otherwise useful annotation blog failed to replay through the page's own move generator, reaching an illegal move between move 24 and move 36. The prose is citable; the move list is not. Game scores now come from pgnmentor player collections and are replay-verified before any FEN is derived. This is the second time in this project a printed score has failed - the first was a UMBC lecture page - and it should be assumed rather than discovered next time.

tool_limitations.item: the shipped puzzle corpus cannot validate a pawn-ending detector
tool_limitations.note: Zero of the 788 shipped puzzle positions is a pure pawn ending, so pawnBreakthrough() fires on none of them and the corpus provides no evidence whatever about its false-positive rate. Any future work on pawn-ending concepts needs a corpus of pawn endings; the 788 will silently return 'no false positives' forever.

tool_limitations.item: attacker counts as a measure of central control
tool_limitations.note: Counting attackers of d4/e4/d5/e5 counts a rook whose line runs through its own man as a piece fighting for the square, which makes the best move in Reti-Capablanca 1924 read as a loss of control. The move-based arm therefore counts pawns and minor pieces only. Even so it cannot separate the two candidate knight moves a GM separates, and that is recorded on the concept rather than tuned around.

measurements.what: How many of the 788 shipped puzzle `why` cards name a motif in chess vocabulary
measurements.conclusion: Quantifies the Education System's surface. The tactical single-move case is covered at 88-100% by findMotifs() and puzzle_words.js and cannot be improved on by this project. The quiet/structural case is at 4-38%, and overall a third of all cards contain no chess vocabulary at all. Research priority is therefore positional, not tactical.

measurements.method: Controlled searchmoves comparison: Stockfish 18, depth 26, 10 threads, 2048MB. For each position every candidate was evaluated inside ONE search of that position, so the only variable is the move. This avoids the separate-search artefacts that make cross-position gambit comparisons unreliable.
findings: Gambit compensation is a measurable quantity, and it can be complete: the Evans Gambit is a pawn down and evaluates to exactly 0.00, so what is surrendered is White's opening edge (0.28) rather than the pawn.

Compensation must be established per gambit, never inferred from the word: the Halloween Gambit gives a knight for a pawn and measures 1.75 worse than the best move, with visible activity and no adequate compensation.
The 'don't bring the queen out early' rule is confirmed in direction and is smaller than its usual phrasing implies: 2.Qh5 costs 0.68 against 2.Nf3.

The claim that the King's Gambit is simply unsound is only partly supported. 2.f4 concedes 0.91 relative to 2.Nf3, which is an inferior line rather than a refuted one - and it evaluates BELOW 2.Qh5, the move beginners are told never to play.

Methodological: openings are one of the few positional areas where controlled comparison is easy, because the alternatives are all legal moves in a single position. This is the same searchmoves technique that failed to isolate outposts, and it works here for exactly that reason.

measurements.method: Stockfish 18, depth 26, MultiPV, on standard opening positions constructed from mainline move orders.

standard IQP after 8.exd4 (Black to move.note: White, who holds the isolani, is +0.14

findings: 'Do not move the same piece twice' is refuted as a rule: 4.Ba4 is best by 0.34 over any alternative in one of the most-played positions in chess.
An isolated queen's pawn is not a weakness on sight - in the standard position the side holding it is slightly better.
Doubled pawns are not a weakness on sight, and the cost of inflicting them is measurable: 4.Bxc6 is 0.34 worse than the quiet retreat, and the side accepting them is exactly equal.
All three surface patterns are ones a naive detector would flag as errors. Each is now a recorded counterexample on its concept.

measurements.method: Constructed positions verified with lib/features.js, then judged by Stockfish 18 at depth 24-26, or by the Syzygy tablebase where the position was small enough.

knight on d5 Black can challenge.detector: d5 not a hole; outposts empty

findings: A centralised advanced knight is not an outpost, and this base's own detector refuses it - the question is definitional, so the feature detector rather than the engine is the instrument that settles it.
An open file confers nothing by itself: symmetric, with a rook of each colour on it, the position is dead level.
A rook on the seventh is not decisive when the rank is empty and the enemy king has luft - the two conditions the concept names are exactly what was removed.
An exposed king is not a losing king; king safety is phase-dependent, and the proven-drawn position has both kings in the open with no shelter at all.

measurements.method: Syzygy tablebase, 3-piece positions differing only in the side to move.
findings: The rule of the square is a statement about the position AND the side to move: the identical board is a draw or a mate in 23 depending only on whose turn it is.
The turn is worth exactly one file, which is why counting files without checking the move is the rule's standard failure.

measurements.method: tools/mass_test.js runs analyzeWithEducation over all 788 shipped puzzle positions with their known solution move, no engine supplied.
findings: Robustness is clean at scale: no crashes, no unfilled templates, no banned phrasings across 788 positions.

The first version of this test reported 99.7% 'positional coverage' and that number was worthless - it counted any positional concept anywhere in a list of six, and the matchers were firing on nearly everything. semi-open-file fired on 83% of positions, open-file on 61%, weak-square on 57%.

Three matchers were tightened against their own concept records as a result: open-file and semi-open-file now require a rook actually on the file, and weak-square reports a hole a minor piece can MOVE TO rather than any hole at all.
The measurement was then changed to the lead concept, which is what the explanation actually says. Lead is a motif 63.5% of the time and positional 36.4%.

That 63.5% is expected and not an achievement: the tactical half delegates to findMotifs, the same detector the shipped layer uses, which explanation_gap.py measured at 65%. The addition is the 36.4%, which is close to the 34% of puzzles where the shipped card layer fell back to comparing numbers.

Agreement with the puzzle generator's independent tagging is 71% on comparable positions. The largest disagreement is hangingPiece, which the generator assigns across a whole solution line while findMotifs judges a single move - an explainable difference in scope rather than a contradiction.

CAVEAT ON THE WHOLE TEST: these are tactical puzzle positions selected for having one best move. They are not a representative sample of quiet positions, which is where a positional explanation layer would most need to be judged, and this base has no such corpus.

measurements.method: Mined 1576 real positions from the puzzle corpus for concept features with lib/features.js, validated 42 of them with Stockfish 18 at depth 20, and separately replayed two master games through the page's own move generator to derive verified FENs.
findings: Two master games were verified end to end rather than transcribed: Capablanca-Tartakower 1924 (103 plies) and Nimzowitsch-Salwe 1911 (77 plies) both replayed legally through the page's own move generator, so every derived FEN is checked rather than remembered.

Testing against those games immediately exposed three false positives that the tactical corpus had not: bad-bishop fired on Nimzowitsch's BLOCKADING bishop, outpost fired on Capablanca's opponent's rim knight on a5, and isolated-queen-pawn fired on a lone d-pawn in a pure rook ending. All three are fixed.

A fourth and more structural problem surfaced with them: ordering by informativeness let a LOW-confidence claim lead. A low-confidence claim must never be the headline, and the sort now demotes them regardless of how interesting the concept would be if true.

Most mined positions are too sharp to isolate a positional concept - the corpus is tactical puzzles - so 13 of them are recorded as AMBIGUOUS examples whose notes say the feature is present and the position is decided by tactics. That is an honest use of them rather than a wasted one.

The depth needle moved very little (0.61 to 0.63) for 21 added positions, which is the real scale of the remaining gap: 129 board-level concepts would need several hundred positions to reach high completeness.

measurements.method: Compared this system's motif detection against the puzzle generator's independent theme tagging on 649 comparable positions, first reading only the solution's first move and then reading the whole solution line.
findings: The apparent false negatives were almost entirely a SCOPE mismatch, not a detection failure. The generator tags themes across a whole solution; the API was reading one move. A combination's fork frequently lands on move three.
Reading the line lifts direct agreement from 77.0% to 96.5%, with only hanging-piece (23) still diverging.

This was a real capability gap in the API rather than a measurement artefact: a caller explaining a combination could not get its motifs. analyzeWithEducation now accepts a `line`, reports motifs per ply, and says which move produced each one.

The residue in the mass test - king-attack 134, sacrifice 119, pawn-breakthrough 86, removing-the-defender 67, perpetual-check 52 - are generator themes computed from the line's EVALUATION rather than by motif detection, so they have no findMotifs equivalent. That is expected and is already documented in tools/motif_map.json.

measurements.method: Added a mechanical quietness test to Layer 3; widened the prospector to 17 concepts with a strong quiet-position preference; verified 13 Zurich 1953 games by replay; harvested quiet positions from them; and searched for positions where a concept's feature is present and its HOLDER is worse.
findings: Quietness is measurable and worth measuring: 22% of the tactical corpus is quiet by the test that the side to move has no check and no winning capture.
Quiet is NOT balanced. Of 62 prospected quiet positions, 29 were still decided by more than three pawns. Those are recorded as ambiguous examples rather than discarded or overclaimed.

Master games break matchers that a tactical corpus does not. Testing against Reshevsky-Petrosian and Nimzowitsch-Salwe exposed the passed-pawn matcher leading on a blockaded pawn and the luft matcher leading where no enemy piece could reach the back rank. Both are now guarded on the concepts' own stated conditions.

Searching for positions where the feature-HOLDER is worse produced only 5 hits from 37 candidates, which is itself informative: in master play a feature is usually held by the side it is helping, so negative evidence is genuinely scarce and cannot be mined in bulk.
Reading the whole solution line rather than its first move lifted mass-test motif detection from 63.5% to 83.5% and agreement with the generator from 71.1% to 89.0%.

measurements.method: Built corpus/annotated_positions.json: positions where a reputable human source names the concept, FENs derived by replaying the whole game through the page's own move generator, and Stockfish used only to verify the annotated move. tools/corpus_check.py validates provenance and runs the real API against every entry.

results.at_start: 0 primary, 0 secondary, 3 false negatives on the first three entries

findings: The first run scored 3 of 3 FALSE NEGATIVES. Human-grounded ground truth found in one sitting what 1576 mined positions and 13 master games had not.

A real Layer 3 BUG: the weak-pawn test counted a pawn on the SAME RANK on an adjacent file as a defender. Pawns capture diagonally forward, so c5 and d5 cannot defend each other - they are the definition of hanging pawns, and the bug hid them. Fischer-Spassky 1972 game 6, where the annotation says outright 'we've reached a position with hanging pawns', reported nothing weak at all.

Fixing that overcorrected: every home-rank pawn became 'undefendable', which is literally true and useless. Qualified by requiring the file to be open on the opponent's side, which is the classical weak-pawn definition.

Restraint is NOT measurable as a drop in legal moves. After Fischer's 30.h4, annotated 'restricting the knight on h7 even further', the knight's move count is UNCHANGED - h4 does not remove g5, it makes g5 unsafe. The matcher now counts destinations not attacked by a pawn.
Two concepts were missing entirely and the corpus exposed both: hanging-pawns, and pawn-break as distinct from pawn-breakthrough (a structural break versus a sacrifice to force a passer).

The two-weaknesses file-distance threshold was my guess. I demanded 3 files on the record's wording 'the far side of the board'; the textbook game has them on a and c, two files apart, both on the queenside. Calibrated to the canonical example.

The API was MATCHING concepts and then slicing them off the returned list because low confidence sorts last and the display cap is six. Added concepts_all: a display cap must not double as a claim that nothing else was found.

Engine verification came back MIXED and is recorded as a finding rather than a filter: 20.e3 and 20.e4 are the engine's first choice, 9.Nxc6 its second by 0.05, 30.h4 its third by 0.40, and 24.b4 - annotated 'the decisive pawn break' - is not in its top three.

measurements.method: Targeted the seven concepts the previous checkpoint named as lacking human grounding - initiative, king safety, centre control, static-vs-dynamic, piece coordination, transformation of advantages and the pawn breakthrough. Annotations were found first and positions second, never the other way round. Game scores were taken from a database (pgnmentor player files) rather than from the annotating page, because six of seven move orders printed by one otherwise useful blog failed to replay; every score used here was replayed end to end through blind-chess.html's own move generator, and every claim was then re-measured with Stockfish 18 at depth 20-22 with MultiPV 3.

results.new_detectors: centralSquareControl, kingZoneAttackers, pawnBreakthrough (Layer 3); center-control, king-safety, king-attack, pawn-breakthrough (Layer 4)
results.firing_rates_over_788_positions: center-control 20.3%, king-attack 1.5%, king-safety-by-count 1.1% of king-sides, king-safety-by-bare-shield 12.4% of king-sides, move-based centre 7.1%, move-based shield damage 2.6%, pawn-breakthrough 0.0%

findings: SIX of seven blog-printed 'full move orders' failed to replay. Only Capablanca-Mattison 1929 survived; Janowsky-Alapin, Rubinstein-Maroczy, Pillsbury-Marco, Havasi-Capablanca and Chekhover-Rudakovsky all reached an illegal move. Prose from such a page can still be cited; its move list cannot. Every score in this corpus now comes from a database and is replay-verified.

A REAL LAYER 3 BUG, found by a corpus position and nothing else. Wade-Korchnoi 1960 has a black pawn on e5 with no d- or f-pawn at all and a white pawn on e4 in front of it, and the detector called it BACKWARD - so the explanation of the most famous pawn breakthrough in the corpus led with 'Black's pawn on e5 cannot advance'. Two causes: the 'is it behind its neighbours' test returns false both when the neighbours are all advanced and when there are none, and the advance square was never checked for occupancy. A pawn with no neighbours is isolated; a pawn blocked by an enemy pawn is rammed. Fixed with a regression test.

THE CHECKER SCORED NEGATIVE EXAMPLES BACKWARDS. corpus_check.py had one rule - is the annotated concept the lead - which scores a negative example as a success exactly when the system has failed it. The bug was invisible while the corpus was all positive, and became live the moment negative entries existed. Now three roles, three standards.

AND THEN THE NEGATIVE EXAMPLES PASSED VACUOUSLY. Both new negatives passed because neither concept had a matcher: nothing could have reported them. A negative example for an undetectable concept is not evidence, and the checker now says so in those words. Writing a king-attack matcher turned one of them into a real test, which it passes.

RAW ATTACKER COUNTS MISREAD THE CENTRE. On Reti-Capablanca 1924, 18...Ne6 - Keene's recommendation and Stockfish's first choice by 0.39 - makes Black's raw attacker count on the four central squares FALL, from 7 to 6, because the arriving knight blocks a rook x-raying its own bishop. Control is now measured on pawns and minor pieces for the move-based arm. It still cannot tell Ne6 from the game's N6d7, and that is recorded on the record rather than tuned away.

THE ENGINE AND THE ANNOTATOR AGREED FOUR TIMES AND DISAGREED THREE TIMES, and both are kept. Agreements: Botvinnik's 20...Qc7, Keene's 18...Ne6 (+0.39 clear, with the game move outside the top three), Keene's 27...Rxe3, Speelman's 22.Be3, Capablanca's 22.Qxc6, 15.Ng5 and 16.Bf3, and Wade's 38.a5 at +9.17 with the engine's variation identical to this base's own detector's line. Disagreements: 20...Qc7 holds the initiative and is still half a pawn worse; 15...d4 and 16...Nd3 are sound ideas the engine does not rank first. An engine-filtered corpus would have thrown all three away and destroyed the distinction the learner needs.

THE PUZZLE GENERATOR AND THE EDUCATION LAYER MEAN DIFFERENT THINGS BY THE SAME WORDS, measured: the generator tags 86 positions `pawnBreakthrough` and ZERO of them is a pawn ending; it tags 134 `kingAttack` and this base reports 12. Both gaps are the concepts' own registered false-positive traps made numeric, and neither number should move.

FIVE OF THE SEVEN TARGET CONCEPTS CANNOT HAVE A DETECTOR, by their own records, and pretending otherwise would have been the easy way to move the numbers. initiative is 'invisible to a static feature scan'; piece-coordination and transformation-of-advantages are human-only; static-vs-dynamic is not a property of a feature. They now have human ground truth instead, and both the ladder and the corpus checker report the distinction from the records rather than from a list.

A NEGATIVE EXAMPLE ONLY COUNTS IF A DETECTOR COULD HAVE FAILED IT, and the corpus now holds one that could: Smyslov-Botvinnik 1954 after 21.Nc5, where a centralised advanced knight in front of an enemy pawn chain is the outpost pattern as any scan sees it and Botvinnik says twice in his own notes that the piece is badly placed. This base's outpost detector agrees and reports nothing, because ...b6 challenges c5 and no white pawn defends it. Two of the corpus's three negatives are now live tests rather than vacuous ones.

TWO FEATURES THAT ARE CORRECT AND WORTH NOTHING, which is what an ambiguous example is for. Nimzowitsch-Capablanca 1914: Black has doubled c-pawns and is +1.07 with the best move on the board being the one that presses the file they opened. Havasi-Capablanca 1929: White has the bishop pair and the engine's first choice for Black, at +0.40, is the move that trades it off. Both features are reported, both correctly, and this base's wording already refuses to go further - 'doubled pawns are a price, not a verdict'.

THE HUMAN-GROUNDED RUNG WAS MEASURING THE WRONG THING, and it was flattering itself. Its own definition says 'an annotated master position, NOT a mined one', and its implementation accepted any position carrying a named game and a historical origin - so 22 of the 36 concepts it counted were grounded only on positions this system found by running its own Layer 4 over master games. Those positions' own notes already said they 'cannot by itself validate the matcher that found it'. Fixed by adding an `attributed_by` field that names the person who said so, and the number fell from 39 to 17. The looser count is still printed underneath, because a drop that large should be legible rather than silent.

A DETECTOR THAT FLICKERS ON AND OFF ACROSS A GAME A HUMAN CALLS SETTLED. Traced ply by ply through Rubinstein-Salwe 1908 - the game whose annotator says flatly that the e6 bishop is bad - this base reports bad-bishop for exactly ten plies, from 16...Nd7 to 21.Nc5, and then stops, while the bishop's pawn share RISES from 0.67 to 0.83 over the same stretch. The cause is the `scope > 3` guard, which is there to keep Suba's active bad bishop off the list and is what stopped this base calling Nimzowitsch's blockading bishop bad. So the guard is right and the concept is momentary in a way its own record says it should not be. Recorded on the record and pinned at both ends by a test, rather than loosened: raising the threshold would restore two false positives to remove one false negative.

AN EXCEPTION THAT LIVED IN THE RECORD AND IN NONE OF THE WORDING. Capablanca-Thomas, Hastings 1929 is an opposite-coloured-bishop ending that Stockfish scores at -5.06 with White a single pawn up, and this base told a reader 'Opposite bishops are drawish in endgames'. The record's own second exception - 'three files of separation between passed pawns usually wins' - was present in the `exceptions` list and in the master-level wording, and absent from the beginner, intermediate, advanced, short and normal wordings and from the lesson line, which is what a reader actually sees. All six now carry the condition. The test written for it does not forbid the word 'draw', which would be the wrong lesson: it requires the condition to travel with the claim.

REJECTED A GROUNDING RATHER THAN TAKE IT. A FIDE Master's lesson titled 'The Backward Pawn on the Semi-Open File' calls White's c3 pawn backward in Marshall-Tarrasch 1905 and explains it as 'the b2 and d4 pawns sit on adjacent files blocking its advance' - after a capture in which the b2 pawn became the c3 pawn, with c4 empty and controlled by nothing. This base's detector reports no backward pawn at any ply of the sequence and is right by the definition the record takes from Wikipedia. Logged in failed_research_attempts and NOT added: the corpus is ground truth, and grounding a concept on a loose application of its own definition would poison the thing it exists to protect. backward-pawn still has no human grounding.

THE `level` PARAMETER HAD NEVER DONE ANYTHING. The API accepts beginner/intermediate/advanced/master, the README documents it, every concept record carries four texts written for those four readers, and asking for master and for beginner returned the SAME SENTENCE on every position. Cause: wordFor() tried `by_depth[depth]` before `by_level[level]`, and every record carries all three by_depth texts, so the by_level branch was unreachable. 137 records times four texts, written and unread. Found by asking, on the Letelier-Fischer position, why four levels printed one string. tests/test_explanations.js had a comment saying 'level must be able to' change the wording with no assertion under it; there is one now, and the wording varies by level on 99.3% of the 788 shipped positions. Two consequences came with the fix: level feeds the TEACHING half rather than the observation, because the observation must name the square and the level texts are general; and teachingSentence() now prefers a sentence long enough to teach something, because the advanced text for `outpost` opens 'Outpost in the modern sense.' and that label was the whole of what an advanced reader used to get.

A FALSE-POSITIVE TEST THAT BANNED A WORD RATHER THAN A CLAIM. The regression suite failed the new intermediate wording 'ask what the exchange bought before calling them a weakness' because it contains the word 'weakness' - which is the opposite of the fault it guards against. The check now splits the explanation into sentences and only fails a sentence that asserts a verdict without a hedging cue.

measurements.method: Added RANK and CONFIDENCE measurement to tools/corpus_check.py. Reporting a concept and burying it were scored the same before this; for a positive entry the annotated concept is what a human said the position is ABOUT, so its rank in the reported list is a measurement. Then measured the firing rate of every concept over the 788 shipped positions, with the solution move supplied, and compared it with the order the PRIORITY list actually used.

results.mass_test_leads: unchanged: 83.5% tactical, and the positional leads are the same set

findings: HALF THE HUMAN-ATTRIBUTED CONCEPTS WERE INVISIBLE. The API returns six concepts by default. On six of twelve positive corpus entries the concept a named annotator attributed to the position sat at rank 7, 8 or 10 - present in concepts_all, absent from anything a caller reads. Nothing measured this until the corpus did.

TWO CAUSES, AND THE FIRST WAS THE PRIORITY LIST CALLING ITSELF INFORMATIVENESS. Measured firing rates: two-weaknesses 72.5%, weak-square 68.9%, passed-pawn 60.4%, open-file 55.7%, space 53.3% - and all five ranked ahead of king-attack (1.5%), backward-pawn (1.9%), luft (4.8%), pawn-break (4.9%) and hanging-pawns (7.2%). A concept true of three quarters of all positions cannot be the most informative thing about any of them. Reordered by the measurement, with the measurement written into the source and two exceptions stated: passed-pawn, which names a concrete asset and whose 60% is an artefact of a corpus one third endgames, and pawn-breakthrough, whose 0% is scope rather than rarity.

AND THE SECOND WAS A RULE APPLIED TO THE WHOLE LIST INSTEAD OF TO ONE ENTRY. The comparator demoted every low-confidence claim below every medium one. Its comment says the rule is that a low-confidence claim must never be the HEADLINE - one position, not all of them - and every badly-ranked corpus concept was a low-confidence one. Now the lead is chosen that way and everything below it is ordered by informativeness. Mean rank 4.9 -> 2.6, and nothing is outside the six any more.

A METRIC MEASURING ITS OWN MAINTENANCE. mass_test.js decided what counts as 'positional' from a hand-written list that had gone stale: center-control, king-safety, king-attack and pawn-breakthrough were all missing, so when one of them took a slot in the visible six it displaced a counted concept and the headline fell from 96.4% to 94.9%. Now derived from each record's knowledge_type - and the number goes back to 99.4%, which this project has already recorded as a figure worth nothing, so the line now says so out loud and points at the LEAD figures instead.

THE HARDEST NEGATIVE SO FAR, AND IT NEEDED AN API CHANGE TO WRITE DOWN. Nimzowitsch-Salwe, Karlsbad 1911 - the founding game of blockade theory, annotated by Nimzowitsch himself - has his dark-squared bishop on d4 PASSING this base's structural test for a bad bishop: four of its own six pawns on its colour, a share of 0.67 against the 0.60 required. Only the scope guard stops the error, and this base called that bishop bad before the guard existed. Recording the claim needed a `side` field, because BLACK's bishop in the same game is bad in every sense and is correctly reported five moves later - and the API's concepts_all carried no `subjects`, so a caller was told 'bad bishop' and not whose. Fixed in the API, in the checker and in the corpus schema; a whole class of per-side negative was unwritable before.

A 1953 SACRIFICE FOR 'QUALITY OF POSITION' IS A 2026 ENGINE'S FIRST CHOICE BY THREE QUARTERS OF A PAWN. Reshevsky-Petrosian, Zurich 1953: 25...Re6 is Stockfish 18's top move at depth 24, 0.76 clear, and its principal variation plays out the annotation's own plan - 26.Rg3 Ne7 27.Bxe6 fxe6 28.Rf1 Nd5, the knight reaching d5 by the exact route described. Black is still a pawn worse, which is the honest half: the sacrifice rescues a difficult position rather than winning one. Recorded as an AMBIGUOUS example for material-imbalance and named against WHITE: the side up the exchange is the side the reader must conclude nothing about.

measurements.method: Listed the 47 concepts whose own records name a mechanical detector and have no matcher, and built the five best-grounded of them. Each was measured over the 788 shipped positions before it was accepted, and each was tested against the game its concept is usually taught from.

findings: A DETECTOR THAT IMPLEMENTED HALF ITS OWN PRECONDITION. The blockade record says 'an enemy passed OR ADVANCING pawn'. The first version used Layer 3's existing `blockadedPassers`, which is the passed half, and it did not fire on Nimzowitsch-Salwe 1911 - the game the concept is named after, where the pawn being blockaded is a backward e-pawn and Nimzowitsch's own note is that its 'immobility is now greater than ever'. Testing a new detector against the game its concept is taught from caught it immediately. The matcher now requires an enemy pawn with no pawn of its own ahead of it on the file, stopped by one of our PIECES, because a pawn stopped by a pawn is a ram and no piece is being spent.

A GEOMETRY THAT FIRED ON 43% BECAUSE IT ARRIVED NOWHERE. `battery` written to its record's bare precondition - two aligned line pieces with a square beyond them - fired on 43% of positions, because two rooks stacked behind their own pawns satisfy it and combine nothing. Requiring the line to reach an enemy man or the enemy half brings it to 24.4%.

AND ONE DETECTOR WRITTEN, MEASURED AND REFUSED. `strong-square` implemented exactly to its record's two preconditions fires on 80.1% of the 788 positions - the `semi-open-file` failure this project has already made once - and it is a third name for a fact already reported twice, since `weak-square` is the same square from the defender's side and `outpost` is the same square with a piece on it. The record's own note says an outpost and a strong point are really the same thing. Removed rather than shipped, with the measurement on the record and a test that keeps it unimplemented.

THREE SUITES ASSERTED A MISSING DETECTOR AS A VIRTUE. tests/test_api.js, tools/api_audit.js and tests/test_explanations.js all demonstrated the 'no forced label' refusal on BARE KINGS, requiring that the position license nothing. But bare kings is where the most certain statement in chess is available - neither side can force mate - and saying nothing there is a gap, not a refusal. Adding `insufficient-material` broke all three, which is the correct outcome and not a regression. The refusal is a real principle and is now demonstrated where it really applies: two kings and two blocked e-pawns, a legal position in which no researched concept fits. Found by building a detector, not by reading a test.

THE RULES LAYER, WHICH THIS SYSTEM COULD NEVER SPEAK. Seven concepts whose records name detectors that already existed - check, stalemate, insufficient-material, fifty-move-rule, en-passant, promotion, castling - had no matcher, so a system built to explain chess could not say 'this is stalemate' or 'the fifty-move count is at 92'. They are the one class of claim it can make with certainty. Two guards were needed to keep them from being noise: `castling` is reported for the MOVE rather than for the rights, which almost every opening position has, and `en-passant` only when the capture is actually available, because a FEN carries the target square whether or not any pawn can use it.

A RECORD WITH TWO TRAPS, WHERE THE FIRST IS ONLY AVOIDED BY HONOURING THE SECOND. `loose-piece` warns that 'reporting every undefended piece would flag most positions and teach nothing' and, separately, that 'it only matters when a FORCING move can reach it'. A detector written to the preconditions plus the obvious guard - is there a move after which this can be won - fired on 66.8% of the 788 tactical positions and 40.6% of the annotated master corpus, because 'undefended and attackable' describes most pieces. Requiring the move to be a check or a capture brings it to 34.9% and 34.4%, and the agreement between two unrelated corpora is the sign that it is measuring the position rather than the corpus. The first trap was the symptom; the second was the cure, and they are two sentences apart in the same record.

measurements.method: Took the mandate's target directly: the concepts with the broadest, most easily triggered recognition rules, and hunted human annotations that would break them. Three of the four newest detectors - blockade, sacrifice, loose-piece - had no human grounding and no negatives at all while firing on a quarter to a third of positions.
